findings.title: The low-liquidity lottery section is a fixed heuristic, not a source-backed mechanism
findings.evidence: The full section hardcodes liquidity<10000, volume<50000, 24h price change>100%, holders<100, age<7d, then buys after a 50% recent increase with 50% TP/30% SL/1h hold. It cites no dataset, backtest, cost model, point-in-time construction or forced counterparty.
findings.verdict: KILLED_AS_MT5_HYPOTHESIS; retained as negative process evidence
findings.why: A scam/pump label does not explain who must buy after the pump or why a Fusion counterparty cannot stop. The rule buys the condition it calls suspicious and omits spread, gaps, contract survival and listing selection.
findings.fusion_mapping: NO CURRENT EXACT ANALOGUE. Closest surface would be thin/new Fusion share CFDs, but the current 23-symbol universe has no share-CFD listing cohort or point-in-time delisting history.
findings.named_data_gap: Complete Fusion share-CFD symbol history with first/last tradable timestamps, point-in-time contract specs, bid/ask ticks, volume or tick-volume semantics, corporate actions, minimum lot and executable spread/swap.

findings.title: Update cadence determines which transformations are meaningful
findings.evidence: Across the public dead-zone notebook, daily rolling regression fields remained high-turnover despite decay, while subtracting overlapping windows, delta/std normalization and fast sign gates on quarterly fields produced near-zero or negative results. The recurring failure mechanism is cadence mismatch: a slow field is flat between updates, so rolling differences amplify update-day noise.
findings.fusion_mapping: For Fusion FX/metals, weekly CFTC COT and scheduled macro releases must be stamped at first availability and treated as event changes or slow regime states, never fabricated into daily observations. Exact symbols: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, XAUUSD and related mapped futures; H1/D1 decisions only after release; costs from observed Fusion spread, tick value and swap.
findings.point_in_time_constraint: COT reference Tuesday is unavailable until the official Friday release; macro revisions require vintage/first-seen values.
findings.screen_scope: Methodology/code audit only. No new trading hypothesis was registered, so no Stage-A survivor claim or multiplicity trial was created.

findings.title: Correlation budget belongs to economic cores, not syntax or sign flips
findings.evidence: The archive's own dead zones show that negating one anchor did not escape a shared analyst/intraday core (~0.94 correlation), and fresh weak legs could not rescue strong saturated cores. Its postmortem independently identifies correlation-to-book as the binding transition after signal generation.
findings.fusion_mapping: Fusion candidates must be compared on timestamp-aligned net sleeve returns against the existing MT5 book. An exact polarity inversion is a duplicate (absolute correlation one), not independent alpha. Existing consumers include libs/stage15/contribution.py and libs/portfolio/capital_competition.py.
findings.screen_scope: Repository audit found book-relative/absolute-correlation consumers already present; the finding changes search emphasis, not a gate or threshold.

findings.title: External research state must be snapshotted before access disappears
findings.evidence: The archive lost platform access after its last normal session and had no durable points/rank/leaderboard snapshot or lock trace. The author explicitly identifies 'I can always look it up later' as the costliest process error.
findings.fusion_mapping: For public MT5 leaderboards/competitions, capture dated public histories, rule versions, failure cohorts and source availability; a current winner screenshot is never a history.
findings.point_in_time_constraint: Capture first_seen and source timestamp separately; disappearance is not evidence of a prior value.
